summary: Overapplied smoothing credit after interleaved postbacks leads to negative mid-cycle balance
description: Issue summary: Customer reported their org balance went negative mid-cycle after an automated credit was applied. Impact: customer lost access to burst capacity for ~3 hours; billing shows a -$1,240 credit line on 2026-03-11 which they did not expect. Environment: production, us-west cluster; hybrid ingestion (batch jobs + realtime webhook postbacks).
impact: Reduced capacity access for DataSail's ingestion pipelines; they reported jobs failing with 402 for ~3 hours. Financial: negative invoice line and unexpected credit memo causing confusion and accounting discrepancies.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a batch embedding job that posts usage in hourly windows to /usage/postback from worker pool A with timezone set to America/Los_Angeles
2) At the same time, send realtime streaming tokens postbacks from service B with UTC timestamping and a 5-7 minute delay
3) Trigger the hourly smoothing/aggregation job (billing-aggregator v2) which de-duplicates and smooths hourly slots
4) Observe that overlapping postbacks are assigned to two adjacent hourly slots and smoothing is applied twice, generating an over-credit on the affected hour
logs: billing-aggregator INFO 2026-03-11T08:00:03Z processed window 2026-03-11T07:00:00Z-08:00:00Z: effective_count=12450 adjusted_for_smoothing=11800
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: deduplication key mismatch between batch and realtime postbacks (different event ids + timezone rounding) caused the aggregator to treat them as distinct and then smoothing applied on both slots.
Checked ingestion pipeline traces in X-Ray: found duplicate postbacks with identical payloads but different 'received_at' and 'source' fields.
Billing aggregator's smoothing logic uses epoch-hour rounding to nearest 30s which can flip when postback delays cross daylight savings boundaries or when source uses local tz offsets.
Safe rollback considered: disable smoothing for 1 hour for the org; but that may surface raw per-event noise to ledger. Need a patch to dedupe by (org_id, job_id, input_hash) before smoothing.
customer_message: We saw a -$1,240 credit on our mid-cycle statement on 2026-03-11 and then several of our scheduled jobs failed due to insufficient capacity. Please restore capacity and explain the credit calculation; our accounting needs a corrected invoice for audit.
support_actions: Provisioned temporary burst credit for DataSail to restore jobs (ticketed as internal credit ref INT-20412), effective 2026-03-12T18:00:00Z
Escalated to billing-engineering and metering team at 2026-03-12T19:10:00Z
Requested detailed ingestion traces from customer; customer provided batch job IDs and webhook delivery logs

next_steps: 1) Merge PR #842 after unit + canary tests (owner: billing-team).
2) Re-run hourly aggregation for 2026-03-11 06:00-10:00 in replay mode for org_id=datasail (dry-run first, then ledger write after validation).
3) If reprocessing reduces over-credit, issue corrective invoice and clear negative balance; else issue manual adjustment and document rationale.
4) Add a monitoring alert that detects >20% delta between raw-postbacks and smoothed_count for an hourly slot for any org.
5) Follow up with DataSail CS and provide a reconciliation spreadsheet and convectional explanation for audit.
